key_insight: Turbulence closure and inflow uncertainty generally dominate street-canyon predictions, but reducing other uncertainties reveals solar effects under weak ventilation, while vegetation already contributes significantly at typical uncertainty levels.
engineering_relevance: Urban exposure studies should constrain turbulence and boundary-condition inputs while resolving thermal and vegetation effects near roads and canyon walls.
method: Run RANS simulations of a two-dimensional street canyon in two ventilation regimes.
Train a PCA–multilayer-perceptron surrogate for velocity, temperature, and concentration fields.
Apply global Sobol analysis to 24 uncertain inputs while progressively narrowing nonthermal, nonvegetation uncertainties.
evidence_signal: Under weak ventilation, solar forcing dominates temperature variance when other uncertainties are halved and concentration variance when quartered; under strong ventilation, canopy effects never exceed closure-constant effects, even with the dominant constant constrained to ±5%.
watch_item: The thresholds come from a surrogate-assisted, two-dimensional RANS study and may not transfer directly to three-dimensional urban geometries.
paper_title: When does boundary-condition uncertainty outweigh thermal and vegetation effects in street canyon flow? A global sensitivity analysis of input uncertainty
